apps._desc: Apps — Admin panel card: app updates and the app installer (with its list of changes).
apps.inst_intro: Paste the compose file from the app's repository (e.g. from GitHub). The installer adapts it to the server: data in {appdata} (covered by backups), a fixed version instead of “latest”, free ports, automatic start and time zone. You will see every change before saving.
apps.inst_adapted_placeholder: The compose appears here after “Adapt”. You can still edit it.
apps.inst_changes_none: Nothing — the compose already fits the server.
apps.inst_need_name: Enter the app name, e.g. immich.
apps.inst_need_compose: Paste the app's compose into the left box.
apps.inst_confirm:
Create the app “{name}”?

The server will create the folders app/{name} and app-data/{name}, save the compose and check it. You will start the app in Dockge afterwards.
apps.inst_working: The server is creating folders and checking the compose…
apps.srv_no_answer: The server does not answer — the “if-aplikacje” task is probably not installed. In the server terminal: sudo if-server → Upgrade.
apps.srv_timeout: The server did not finish within 90 s. Check later in Dockge whether the app appeared.
apps.upd_intro: The installed and the newest stable version of each app (no beta/rc/dev). Versions are checked once a day — “Check now” asks right away. {update} is done by the server: app backup, new version, start and a check that it works — if not, back to the previous version together with the data. “Undo” restores only the compose file (for advanced users, then Dockge).
apps.local_image_tip: An image built on this server, e.g. a test version. It is not in any registry, so there is nothing to check.
apps.major_tip: A new version in a different line (e.g. 11.8 → 13.0). Read “What's new”, and for databases and apps with data make a backup of the data first.
apps.undo_tip: Restore compose.yaml from the last backup (backups: {n})
apps.note_wordpress: WordPress itself, plugins and themes are updated in the WordPress panel (Dashboard → Updates). A new image only changes PHP and the Apache server.
apps.note_database: Database — back up the database before a new major version.
apps.undo_confirm:
Restore compose.yaml for “{name}” from the last backup?

Then click “Update” in Dockge to start the restored version.
apps.upd_steps_backup: First I will back up this app, then download and start the new version and check that it works. If it does not work, I will go back to the previous version together with the data from this backup.
apps.upd_steps_nobackup: WARNING: backup is not set up (Admin panel → Backup) — the update runs without a backup. If the new version does not work, I will go back to the previous version, but changes in the data cannot be undone.
apps.upd_major_warn: This is a major version change — read “What's new” first.
apps.upd_no_answer: The server does not answer — the “if-aplikacje” task is probably not installed (sudo if-server → Upgrade).
apps.chg_version_removed: Removed the outdated “version” line — Docker no longer needs it.
apps.chg_env_path_needs_env: {service}: data path from {key} — paste the .env file to adapt it.
apps.chg_file_stays: {service}: the file {src} stays next to the compose — upload it to the app folder (app/{name}).
apps.chg_volume_moved: {service}: data from the hidden volume “{src}” → {target} (visible in files, covered by backups).
apps.chg_version_pinned: {service}: version “{old}” → {new} (fixed version — updates work and you know what is installed).
apps.chg_version_unknown: {service}: could not find the image version — “{old}” stays.
apps.chg_container_name: {service}: container name “{name}” (readable in alerts and Status).
apps.chg_restart: {service}: automatic start after a server restart (restart: unless-stopped).
apps.chg_port_no_free: {service}: port {port} is taken and there is no free one in the range {range} — change it by hand.
apps.job_app_ready: The app “{nazwa}” is ready: compose in app/{nazwa}, data in app-data/{nazwa}. Start it in Dockge (“Deploy”).
apps.job_app_exists: The app “{nazwa}” is already on the server (folder app/{nazwa}). Nothing was changed.
apps.job_compose_rejected: Docker did not accept the compose: {opis}
apps.job_backup_busy: A backup or restore is in progress — try again when it ends.
apps.job_backup_no_answer: The backup task does not answer (if-backup). In the server terminal: sudo if-server → Upgrade.
apps.job_backup_failed: The app backup before the update failed: {blad}
apps.job_backup_timeout: The app backup before the update takes too long — I stopped waiting.
apps.job_restore_timeout: Restoring data takes too long — I stopped waiting.
apps.job_compose_missing: No compose file found for the app “{stos}”.
apps.job_no_new_compose: The page did not send the new compose.
apps.job_pull_failed: Could not download the new version ({blad}). Nothing was changed — the app runs as before.
apps.job_rolled_back: The new version does not work ({powod}). I restored the previous version — the app runs as before the update.
apps.job_rolled_back_backup: The new version does not work ({powod}). I restored the previous version and the data from the backup {kopia} — the app runs as before the update.
apps.job_rollback_failed: The new version does not work ({powod}), and after going back to the previous version the app did not start either ({opis}). Check it in Dockge.
apps.job_rollback_failed_backup: The new version does not work ({powod}), and after going back to the previous version and the data from the backup {kopia} the app did not start either ({opis}). Check it in Dockge.
apps.job_updated_backup: The app “{nazwa}” runs version {wersja}. Backup from before the update: {kopia}.
apps.job_reason_start_timeout: the app did not start within {minuty} min ({lista})
apps.stage_rollback: Going back to the previous version

backup._desc: Backup — Admin panel card: disk and schedule settings, making a backup, restoring.
backup.no_disk_list: The server has not prepared the disk list yet.
backup.pick_disk_hint: We recommend an external (USB) disk — the backup survives a server failure.
backup.note_empty: Empty disk — it must be prepared (formatted) first.
backup.note_windows: Disk in Windows format — not suitable for backups (it would have to be formatted, which erases its contents).
backup.note_system: This is the system disk — a backup will not protect against its failure. We recommend an external (USB) disk.
backup.note_internal: Internal disk — we recommend an external (USB) disk.
backup.freq_title: How often and how many backups
backup.important_text: Depending on the space you have, choose the number of backups and how often they are made.
backup.count: How many backups to keep — of each kind
backup.count_note: Counted separately: “Everything” backups and backups of each app (e.g. with 7 — seven “Everything” backups and, separately, seven backups of the mail app alone). When there are more backups of a kind, the oldest one is deleted. A backup of one app never deletes backups of another app or “Everything” backups.
backup.scanning: The server is checking disks… (this may take a minute)
backup.scan_no_answer: The server does not answer. In the server terminal: sudo if-server → Upgrade (sets up the backup task).
backup.need_disk: First choose a disk in Settings and save them.
backup.last_none: No backup has been made yet.
backup.last_ok: Last backup{part}: {when} — successful ({size}, {minutes} min). Backups on disk: {copies}.
backup.scope_note: Automatic backups also follow these ticks (Settings → how often).
backup.first_too_big: The first backup (approx. {size}) will not fit on this disk ({free} free).
backup.first_fits: First backup: approx. {size} · free on disk: {free}. Later backups only take what has changed
backup.fits_times: — there is room for a full backup about {n} times
backup.fits_times_over: — there is room for a full backup more than {n} times
backup.no_copies: There are no backups on the disk yet (or the list is not refreshed — “Check disks” in Settings).
backup.last_restore_ok: Last restore: {app} from the backup {copy} ({when}). Data from before the restore: {moved}
backup.restore_intro: Restores apps (files, data and volumes) to their state in the selected backup. Current data is not deleted — it goes to {folder}.
backup.server_restore: The whole server after a failure (new Debian) is restored by the {program} program.
backup.confirm_all:
Restore ALL apps to their state from {copy}?

Each app goes back to its state in this backup — later changes disappear from the apps. The apps are stopped one by one. Their current data is not deleted — it goes to ~/backups/przed-przywroceniem.
backup.confirm_one:
Restore “{app}” to its state from {copy}?

The app will be stopped for a moment. Its current data is not deleted — it goes to ~/backups/przed-przywroceniem.
backup.bkp_msg_disk_missing: The backup disk is not connected. Connect it and try again.
backup.bkp_msg_disk_bad_fs: The selected disk is not suitable for backups (file system). Choose another disk.

modules._desc: Modules — Admin panel card with module tiles (Server kiosk, Port tester).
modules.title: Modules
modules.intro: Add-ons for self-hosted services, made simple for everyone at home. Pick a module to change its settings.
modules.kiosk_desc: A tablet showing server status — temperatures, disks, alerts, a live view of containers (ctop style), container status and internet radio.
modules.ports_desc: Port ranges by app type and a check whether a port on the server is free.
modules.language_desc: Translating the page and the Admin panel, new languages, exporting and uploading language files.

admin_theme._desc: Admin panel appearance — card: colours, fonts, panels, wallpaper, sidebar and buttons, day and night separately.
admin_theme.title: Admin panel appearance
admin_theme.intro: Changes show right away. Save to keep them. “Undo changes” goes back to the last saved look, and “Default look” to the look after installation.
admin_theme.mode_label: You are editing the look of
admin_theme.mode_note: Day and night have separate settings. Choosing a mode also switches the Admin panel, so you see what you are editing.
admin_theme.accent_alt_tip: Tile headings in Admin panel tabs (e.g. “Temperature thresholds”) and window titles. One control changes headings across the whole Admin panel.
admin_theme.surface_tip: Fallback window colour. Windows in the Admin panel take their look from the Start page → Appearance → Dialog windows (day and night separately) — change their colour there.
admin_theme.input_text_tip: Text typed in form fields and drop-down lists in the Admin panel. The hint in an empty field uses a lighter version of this colour.
admin_theme.switch_confirm: Unsaved appearance changes will be lost. Switch mode?
admin_theme.reset_confirm_day: Restore the default Admin panel look (day)? Saved appearance settings for this mode will be removed.
admin_theme.reset_confirm_night: Restore the default Admin panel look (night)? Saved appearance settings for this mode will be removed.

general._desc: General settings — Admin panel card: page title, server name, administrator PIN, auto logout, logo.
general.title: General settings
general.subtitle: Description / subtitle
general.host_tip: Like the start page's domain, e.g. iflab — you open it at http://iflab. Links to Dockge, Cockpit and apps use this name. if-server fills it in during installation (server name). You can also open the page by its IP number — it works the same.
general.language_tip: Language of the page and the Admin panel. Missing translations show in English. After saving, the page reloads.
general.auto_logout_tip: When nobody touches the mouse or keyboard for this long, the page and the Admin panel log out by themselves — the next edit asks for the PIN. Applies to every browser, also after it is closed.
general.translator_tip: A card for translating the page and managing languages (editor, new language, export, file upload). When on — the {icon:languages} icon in the page menu (bottom of the sidebar) and a tile in Modules. Choosing a language works without the module too.
general.formats_note: How the page shows the date, time, numbers and temperature. “By language” — as is usual in the page language.
